item: Unlock: the page says what the passphrase check is recovering, and the check no longer freezes the app while it does (rank 5, phase 0)
key_paths: src/api/unlock.py; src/api/startup_status.py; src/monitoring/forensics.py; src/static/unlock.html; src/static/unlock.js; tests/test_unlock_recovery_progress.py; tests/test_failed_open_wal_facts.py; tests/unlock_recovery_node_test.js
summary: Unlocking an encrypted store left with a large -wal showed only an elapsed clock for as long as the passphrase check ran (24.7 s on the field's S3 boot), and sqlcipher3's close() held the GIL through the write-back so the whole process, the event loop included, stood still. While the check runs on a log of at least 64 MiB the unlock page now says how big the log is, what this machine's own last measured recovery implies (named, absent when there is none, never a constant) and the seconds elapsed, through GET /api/system/unlock-progress (the one path a locked app adds: numbers only, inactive outside an attempt, cleared in a finally); forensics keeps last_recovery apart from last_unlock and carries it across boots and into the diagnostics block. The verify connection checkpoints through execute before it closes (measured: close() 2.1 s with a 2.1 s worst gap, execute 1.7 s with 0.01 s), so the page can be answered meanwhile. A wrong passphrase at the right page size still pays the close-time checkpoint inside connect (measured about 1.5 s per GiB, once per log); no call-site fix exists, connect.py is unchanged and four facts are pinned in tests/test_failed_open_wal_facts.py. Sentences in 12 locales. Browser-unverified until a Chromium walk.
